clue.text: Highland area priest in collar, prickly sort

indicators.note: the area and the priest are placed inside the word for collar, as the clue's 'in' directs

parts.note: to collar someone is to catch or seize them
Ross is a district of the Scottish Highlands, as in Ross and Cromarty

explanation.surface: A grumpy, thorny cleric in the Highlands is described, his neck stiff in a clerical collar.
explanation.walkthrough: 'collar' looks like a dog collar for the priest, but it is a verb meaning catch, which wraps ROSS and P. ROSS is part of the historic Highland county of Ross and Cromarty.
explanation.definitionFit: A grumpy, irritable person is a bad-tempered sort, easily provoked like something thorny.

indicators.note: deployed in means positioned within, so the Roman numeral sits inside the word for charge

parts.note: to have care of something is to have it in your charge
D is the Roman numeral for 500

explanation.surface: A military unit of five hundred is sent out under someone's command.
explanation.walkthrough: 'deployed' suggests troops, but here 'deployed in' just places D inside CARE.
explanation.definitionFit: A cadre is a core group of trained personnel, a body or unit like a military corps.

parts.note: to be off is to have set out or started on something
a bound is a leap or spring

explanation.surface: Someone set off on a journey with a jump to take up a question.
explanation.walkthrough: 'issue' looks like a matter for debate but means children, as in 'died without issue'.
explanation.definitionFit: Children or descendants are a person's progeny, legally called their issue.

parts.note: suggests concert-goers spellbound by music, but describes people who walk about while asleep

explanation.surface: Concert audiences at the Proms look spellbound by the music.
explanation.walkthrough: Promenaders are standing audiences at the BBC Proms, London concerts; here they are simply people walking about.
explanation.definitionFit: Sleepwalkers stroll in a trance-like state, unconscious of their surroundings.

parts.note: U is the film-classification abbreviation for universal
spice is what adds interest or zest

explanation.surface: A sign, a general truth, a fascinating element.
explanation.definitionFit: A portent or augury foretells events, as in the Roman watching of birds.

clue.text: Chopin's first study, couched in masterful rhythm

indicators.note: first takes just the opening letter of the composer's name
couched in means lying inside, so the word for study is set within the word for masterful

parts.note: ace means expert or masterful
a den is a private study

explanation.surface: Chopin's first étude is set in skilful rhythm.
explanation.walkthrough: The music picture makes 'study' an étude, but it is a room, DEN, lying inside ACE.
explanation.definitionFit: A cadence is the rise and fall or beat of sound, a measured flow.

clue.text: Some German Luger backfired? A feature of the arm?

indicators.note: a gun that backfires sends things the wrong way, so the run of letters is read backwards
only some of the letters of the phrase German Luger are used, a run lying across the two words

explanation.surface: A German pistol misfires, and the question is whether the injury is to the arm.
explanation.walkthrough: The run ANLU spans the end of 'German' and the start of 'Luger'; 'backfired' turns it round.
explanation.definitionFit: This is one of the two long bones of the forearm, so it is a part of the limb.

clue.text: He's landed in a hole, bit of a dilemma

parts.note: a lair is an animal's den or hole

indicators.note: bit of takes just a small piece, the first letter, of dilemma

explanation.surface: A man has fallen into a hole, in a bit of a fix.
explanation.walkthrough: A LAIRD is a Scottish landowner; 'landed' means owning land, not arriving. 'in' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: A Scottish estate owner belongs to the gentry with property, the landed class.

definitions.meaning: in a manner wholly devoid of art, art being work or skill
in a simple, guileless, sincere way

explanation.surface: Someone completely idle, frankly speaking.
explanation.walkthrough: The first definition reads ART LESS LY: in a way totally lacking art.
explanation.definitionFit: Doing something naively and without guile is doing it sincerely, without craft or skill.

clue.text: Baffling line in bull? I get over one's head

indicators.note: baffling means confounding, so these letters are thrown into confusion

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A line in nonsense goes over one's head, leaving one baffled.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Baffling' looks like the definition but rearranges LINEINBULLIGET; 'bull' is nonsense on the surface.
explanation.definitionFit: Something beyond comprehension is too hard to understand, going above you.

clue.text: Grazed back has same blotchy smears

indicators.note: back tells us to read the word for grazed in the reverse direction

parts.note: cattle that grazed have fed

indicators.note: blotchy suggests patchy disorder, so the letters of same are mixed up

explanation.surface: An animal's scraped back looks the same as some blotchy marks.
explanation.walkthrough: 'back' turns FED into DEF; 'blotchy' rearranges SAME into AMES; 'has' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: To smear someone is to slander them, damaging their good name.

annotationWithheld.why: Clue held as 'He might make you (7)' for DENTIST appears cut short; no wordplay or full cryptic definition can be read from these words and no source gives the rest.

clue.text: Compensation in the end, sacrificing Rook

indicators.note: sacrificing means giving something up, so the letter for the chess piece is dropped

parts.note: an expiration is a termination or end
R is the chess abbreviation for rook

explanation.surface: A chess player sacrifices a rook at the end of a game to win something back.
explanation.walkthrough: The chess picture of sacrificing a rook hides the plain removal of R from EXPIRATION; 'in' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Atonement makes amends for a wrong, a kind of moral repayment for it.

annotationWithheld.why: Clue held as 'Push, say-demand (5)' for NUDGE: 'Push' defines it, but no reading of 'say-demand' gives NUDGE, so the clue looks misread or garbled and no source confirms the printed text.

parts.note: C is the abbreviation for club, as in card suits
a limb is a member of the body; the 's is a link

explanation.surface: A member of a club makes progress or gets promoted.
explanation.definitionFit: To ascend is to move upward, to go forward or rise.

definitions.meaning: general nature or drift, as in the tenor of a speech
a role played by an actor

explanation.surface: A singer's role in an opera.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Tenor' suggests a singing voice, but means general character or nature.
explanation.definitionFit: Nature or quality is one's essential makeup; a role in a play is an actor's persona.

parts.note: reads as a short training course, but means a quick snack taken as a small meal course in mid-morning

explanation.surface: A short course to bring one's skills up to date.
explanation.walkthrough: ELEVENSES is the British mid-morning tea or coffee break with a biscuit.
explanation.definitionFit: A mid-morning snack is a short break that refreshes, a small meal or course.

clue.text: Fan's left in police officer's custody

indicators.note: in, with custody, places the side word inside the officer's title

parts.note: super is short for a superintendent, a senior police officer
port is the left side of a ship

explanation.surface: A fan has been left in police custody by a senior officer.
explanation.walkthrough: SUPER is British slang for a police superintendent; PORT, left on a ship, goes inside it. 'custody' completes the containment picture.
explanation.definitionFit: A fan is a follower or backer of a team.

parts.note: angelica is an aromatic herb whose stems are candied
L is the abbreviation for lake on maps

explanation.surface: A pretty scented herb grows beside a lake.
explanation.definitionFit: Something heavenly or saintly is beautiful, charming and sweet.

clue.text: He's got a job at last

definitions.text: He's got a job at last

parts.words: He's got a job at last
parts.note: suggests someone finally employed, but describes a worker whose job is done on a shoemaker's last

explanation.surface: Someone long unemployed has finally been hired.
explanation.walkthrough: A last is the foot-shaped block on which shoes are made or mended.
explanation.definitionFit: A shoe mender works with leather on a foot-shaped form.

clue.text: Items in the wash duly ran with boiling

indicators.note: boiling suggests churning agitation, so the letters of the two words are mixed up

explanation.surface: Clothes in a hot wash ran their colours as expected.
explanation.walkthrough: 'boiling' rearranges DULYRAN; 'with' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Clothes and linen being washed or waiting to be cleaned make up a household's washing.

indicators.note: discarding is throwing away a card, so the letter for spades is removed

parts.note: slippy is a word for smooth and slippery
S is the abbreviation for spades, the card suit

explanation.surface: A card player discards a spade with smooth, bold confidence.
explanation.walkthrough: The card-game picture of 'discarding Spade' is a deletion of S from SLIPPY.
explanation.definitionFit: Cheeky and impudent describes someone speaking with bold nerve.

indicators.note: returned means sent back, so the word for ring is written backwards

parts.note: to toll is to ring a bell

explanation.surface: A ring sent back inside a package.
explanation.walkthrough: 'parcel' looks like a noun but is the verb, as in parcel out; 'in' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: To parcel out is to share out or distribute in portions.

indicators.note: in places the letter for born inside the word for car

parts.note: a limo is a large car, a limousine
B is the abbreviation for born in records

explanation.surface: A baby delivered in the back of a car during labour.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Confinement' suggests childbirth, matching the surface, but means a state of being held or neglected.
explanation.definitionFit: Limbo is a state of uncertain detention or neglect, a kind of holding place.

clue.text: Capitalist, short oik, in fancy brogues

indicators.note: in places the shortened word inside the rearranged shoe letters
fancy suggests something elaborate or reworked, so the letters of brogues are rearranged
short means cut off at the end, so the final letter of oik is dropped

parts.note: an oik is a British slang word for a boorish, uncouth person

explanation.surface: A money-man calls someone a short lout while wearing fancy leather shoes.
explanation.walkthrough: 'fancy' rearranges BROGUES into BOURGES; 'short' cuts OIK to OI, which goes inside after BOURGE. Brogues are sturdy decorated leather shoes.
explanation.definitionFit: A middle-class person is associated with property and the capitalist order.

parts.note: a side is an interest or party in a dispute

explanation.surface: Banks pay interest, along with building societies.
explanation.walkthrough: 'banks' looks like the financial sense from 'Interest', but means slopes or edges, as in river banks; 'and' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: The edges of a river slope down to the water, forming its flanks.

clue.text: Cart beginning to tip assorted lumber

indicators.note: the beginning to a word is its first letter, so only the opening letter of tip is used
assorted means mixed, so the letters of lumber are scrambled

explanation.surface: A cart is tipped to unload a mixed pile of timber.
explanation.walkthrough: 'beginning to' gives T from 'tip'; 'assorted' rearranges LUMBER into UMBREL.
explanation.definitionFit: A tumbrel is a two-wheeled farm vehicle, famously carrying victims to the guillotine.

indicators.note: about means surrounding, so the word for action goes round the word for rate

parts.note: a deed is an action
bat is an informal word for pace or rate, as in going at a fair bat

explanation.surface: Something was thought over: an action concerning a rate.
explanation.walkthrough: BAT meaning speed is British colloquial, as in 'off at a rare bat'.
explanation.definitionFit: To deliberate over something is to weigh it up or argue it through.

indicators.note: faceless means losing the front, so the first letter of the word for swindler goes

parts.note: a crook is a swindler

explanation.surface: A cheat and a featureless con man.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sharper' looks like a comparative adjective but is a noun: a card sharper, a cheat.
explanation.definitionFit: A cardsharp cheats people, and to fleece or defraud is also its sense.

definitions.meaning: large stoneware drinking jugs decorated with a bearded face

explanation.surface: Stoneware jugs of wine belonging to elderly men.
explanation.definitionFit: The jug was a bellarmine stoneware vessel with a bearded mask; old men are known by their grey whiskers.
